items.title: Third US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle East as Iran targets Bahrain
items.summary: A third American aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, US Central Command said in a social media post Monday, making a dramatic show of military might as President Donald Trump keeps his options open for next steps in the Iran war. It comes as Tehran said Sunday that its forces carried out a drone attack on a US radar system at a helicopter base in the Gulf kingdom of Bahrain.
items.t: Third US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle East as Iran targets Bahrain

items.title: Saudi Arabia replaces military commander after Yemen setbacks
items.summary: Saudi Arabia replaced the commander overseeing its coalition against Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis on Monday after Riyadh's Yemeni allies were forced to withdraw from swathes of territory in a major setback for their campaign against the group.
items.t: Saudi Arabia replaces military commander after Yemen setbacks

items.title: 5 European countries aim to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda
items.summary: A group of European countries announced Monday that they aim to set up a “return hub” in Rwanda where rejected asylum seekers could be sent from next year, a move that they hope will also deter more people from coming. The plan by Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands, which have spearheaded negotiations with non-EU countries, drew immediate criticism from human rights groups.
items.t: 5 European countries aim to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda

items.title: Iran claims another attack targeting U.S. radar site in Bahrain
items.summary: Iran has claimed to hit U.S. radar systems in Bahrain three times in less than a week, but authorities said the first two attacks were intercepted.
items.t: Iran rules out inspections of damaged nuclear sites until war ends

items.title: Ukraine critically damages Kerch Bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia
items.summary:
Photos of bridge, built after 2014 annexation and viewed by Ukraine as illegal, suggest massive steel arch has fallen into water

  • Europe live – follow latest

Ukraine has critically damaged the Kerch Bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia in an overnight missile attack, in what Volodymyr Zelenskyy hailed as an “unprecedented” military operation.

Footage showed a Ukrainian Flamingo cruise missile seconds before it hit the road and railway crossing, followed by an explosion. The strike follows an earlier attack on Monday that targeted an arch across its central section.

Continue reading...
items.t: Ukraine critically damages Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia

items.title: Ukraine strikes major Crimea bridge, Russia retaliates on Kyiv
items.summary: The Kerch Bridge holds symbolism in Ukraine since it was built after Russia's annexation of Crimea in 2014.
items.t: Ukraine strikes major Crimea bridge, Russia retaliates on Kyiv

items.title: Trump arrives in Philippines to kick off Asia trip
items.summary: US President Donald Trump arrived in the Philippines on Tuesday at the tail end of a Southeast Asian summit, with protests awaiting him as he prepares for the first meeting in two years of the Quad group of Indo-Pacific countries. France 24’s correspondent Tommy Walker has the details.
items.t: Trump arrives in Philippines to kick off Asia trip

items.title: Ukraine hails attack on vital Kerch bridge linking Russia and Crimea – Europe live
items.summary:
Zelenskyy praises ‘unprecedented attack’ as the Kremlin says bridge will be restored and will be ‘better than ever’ following strike

  • Ukraine critically damages Kerch bridge

Meanwhile, the Kremlin said its bridge linking occupied Crimea to Russia will be “even better” after it is rebuilt following a large-scale Ukrainian attack that caused significant damage.

“There is, of course, no doubt that the bridge will be restored and will be even better than before,” Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said, quoted by Russian state media.

Continue reading...
items.t: Ukraine hails attack on vital Kerch bridge linking Russia and Crimea – Europe live

items.title: Candidates clash over cost of living in French presidential debate
items.summary: Five of the frontrunners for the French presidential election lined up for the second of this year's debates on Monday night. In an often-rowdy debate, candidates clashed over counterproposals to raise and cut taxes and slash public spending.
items.t: Candidates clash over cost of living in French presidential debate

items.title: France's far-right presidential candidate Le Pen to set out pension plans
items.summary: France's far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen is to set out pension proposals on Tuesday as she seeks to convince investors she can balance one of her most popular electoral pledges ‌with promises to restore order to the public finances. Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) has pledged to allow people ⁠who started work young to retire as early as 60, although it is under pressure to detail how it would ‌do this while also curbing budget deficits.
items.t: France's far-right presidential candidate Le Pen to set out pension plans

items.title: Russia receiving ‘dozens of missiles per month’ from North Korea, says Kyiv
items.summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday that Russia was receiving "dozens of missiles per month" from North Korea and warned that the country was taking advantage of the war to make its weapons "more effective". He called on European allies to send more weapons so that Ukraine can respond "on equal terms" to the threat.
items.t: Russia receiving ‘dozens of missiles per month’ from North Korea, says Kyiv

items.title: Trump in Asia for Putin, Xi summit; possible Kim meeting
items.summary: The president arrived in Manila for the start of a multi-day swing in Asia, where he's scheduled to meet with Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping in a highly anticipated summit. He says he may also meet with North Korea's Kim Jong Un.
items.t: Trump heads to Asia for Putin, Xi summit; possible Kim meeting

items.title: Russia downs over 1,400 Ukrainian drones as Kyiv hits a key bridge in Crimea
items.summary:
Ukraine's forces targeted a key rail and road bridge between Russia and the Crimean Peninsula for a second day. Moscow's forces, meanwhile, fired ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv.

(Image credit: AP Photo/)
items.t: Russia downs over 1,400 Ukrainian drones as Kyiv hits a key bridge in Crimea

items.title: Trump to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin for joint summit
items.summary: President Trump is off for a series of meetings in Asia that will cover trade, security and a rare trilateral meeting with China and Russia.
items.t: Trump to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin for joint summit

items.title: China, Canada agree to further reduce tariffs at APEC summit in Shenzhen
items.summary: China is hosting the 21-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen this week, hoping to use the tech megalopolis to showcase its vision for international trade and development. The summit is also where the international agenda is enacted: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney has met with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, with both leaders agreeing to reduce trade barriers between their countries. Also in this edition: Nvidia reportedly rejects a return of its former CEO Jensen Huang.
items.t: China, Canada agree to further reduce tariffs at APEC summit in Shenzhen

items.title: Deutsche Bank shares drop after reports on mass data leak
items.summary: Shares in Deutsche Bank plunged on Tuesday after international media outlets published reports based on millions of leaked emails and other documents that shine a light on questionable past business practices at the German banking giant.
items.t: Deutsche Bank shares drop after reports on mass data leak

items.title: AFCON 2027 qualifiers: Senegal beat Sudan and close in on qualification
items.summary: Senegal beat Sudan 4–2 on Matchday 4 of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. Senegal top Group J and could secure qualification as early as Tuesday, November 17.
items.t: 2027 AFCON qualifiers: Senegal beat Sudan and close in on qualification

items.title: ‘Line their own coffers’: independent MPs lambast Labor’s last-minute changes to election funding laws
items.summary:
Crossbenchers say the proposals could allow an ‘uncapped amount of money’ to flow to major parties through investment funds

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Independent MPs say the government’s last-minute changes to controversial election funding laws would allow “an uncapped amount of money” to flow to the major parties through investment funds.

The amendments to the incoming federal electoral laws, which the government describes as “technical”, were introduced on Tuesday afternoon and come weeks before they are set to begin operating.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘Line their own coffers’: independent MPs lambast Labor’s last-minute changes to election funding laws

items.title: Communications watchdog leadership reversed findings of draft report into ABC Four Corners program, FoI documents reveal
items.summary:
Documents show draft Acma reports backed reporting of Gold Walkley award-winning journalist Mark Willacy about Australian War Memorial

  • Sign up for Guardian Australia’s free weekly media newsletter here

An investigation by staff of the Australian Media and Communications Authority (Acma) cleared an ABC Four Corners program over its War Memorial reporting – only for the draft report findings to be reversed by the regulator’s leadership, documents released under freedom of information reveal.

Internal correspondence shows the 11th hour backflip forced a “retrofit” of the report which initially said: “Staff are of the preliminary view that the program did not breach the impartiality provision of the [ABC] code [of conduct] with respect to this allegation.”

Sign up to get Guardian Australia’s weekly media diary as a free newsletter

Continue reading...
items.t: Communications watchdog leadership reversed findings of draft report into ABC Four Corners program, FoI documents reveal

items.title: Live: France braces for new day of protests as unions call for nationwide strike
items.summary: France braced for another day of protests Tuesday as unions called for a nationwide strike by public sector workers in a bid to secure pay rises. Youth organisations and Yellow Vest activists are also set to join the demonstrations. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
items.t: Live: France braces for new day of protests as unions call for nationwide strike

items.title: New mass protests expected in France Tuesday as presidential election approaches
items.summary: Unions in France are calling for a strike Tuesday to demand wage increases, with students also expected to join. With under five months to go before the presidential election, FRANCE 24's Monte Francis asks Ariane Bogain, Senior Lecturer in French Politics at Northumbria University, what role the widespread discontent will play in the upcoming vote.
items.t: New mass protests expected in France Tuesday as presidential election approaches

items.title: ‘Disgusted by it’: body of Melbourne Cup race horse found dumped in Sydney skip bin
items.summary:
So You Are placed eighth in race just two weeks ago and was put down after a severe bout of colic

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The body of a horse that placed eighth in Australia’s Melbourne Cup two weeks ago and recently fell ill has been found dumped in skip bin in Sydney.

The horse So You Are, a five-year-old gelding, was put down after it suffered from a severe bout from colic and was taken to hospital on Monday for surgery.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘Disgusted by it’: body of Melbourne Cup race horse found dumped in Sydney skip bin

items.title: Hundreds arrested in anti-Trump protests in Philippines amid anger over Iran war and AI pact
items.summary:
Organisers say up to 10,000 people could join the next round of demonstrations ahead of the US president’s arrival in Manila for the Asean summit

  • Asean and Apec summits – live updates

Hundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against Donald Trump in Manila, as authorities braced for more protests ahead of the US president’s arrival in the city for a leaders’ summit.

Organisers claim as many as 10,000 people will join protests against Trump in the Philippine capital on Tuesday, when he will attend the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit. The crowds are expected to try to walk to the summit site.

Continue reading...
items.t: Hundreds arrested in anti-Trump protests in Philippines amid anger over Iran war and AI pact

items.title: Woman whose baby died after free birth didn’t know she was pregnant with twins, NSW inquest hears
items.summary:
Inquest continues into deaths of four babies born in free births or home births in northern rivers

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A northern rivers mother whose baby died after a free birth did not know she was having twins until she was in labour after having no pregnancy scans, the New South Wales coroner’s court has heard.

The inquest will examine the deaths of four babies born in free births or home births who died in the northern rivers region between 2022 and 2024. It will consider whether the care was reasonable in the circumstances and whether care by an unregistered support worker was reasonable and appropriate before, during and after the birth. Free births are when a person gives birth without a registered health professional present.

Continue reading...
items.t: Woman whose baby died after free birth didn’t know she was pregnant with twins, NSW inquest hears

items.title: David Jones: what went wrong and what happens next? Five takeaways from first creditors meeting
items.summary:
Upmarket retailer, which recorded a net loss of $228m last financial year, has total debt over $400m including $11m owed to staff

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Upmarket retailer David Jones owed hundreds of millions of dollars when it collapsed into administration, after accelerating financial losses and reputational damage threatened its ability to stock shelves for Christmas.

About 500 creditors attended its first meeting on Tuesday, where administrators McGrathNicol started to break down who is owed what, when those left out of pocket will know where they stand, and what ultimately went wrong.

Continue reading...
items.t: David Jones’ total debt is over $400m including millions owed to staff, administrators confirm

items.title: European-made pesticides named in 1,605 poisoning reports in Brazil last year
items.summary:
About a third of cases involved chemicals banned for use on EU farms, according to investigation by Unearthed and Public Eye

Pesticides sold by European chemical companies were named in more than 1,600 poisoning reports in Brazil last year, an investigation has found.

About a third of the cases involved chemicals banned from use on farms in the EU because of the risks they pose to people and the environment. But European companies are not banned from manufacturing these chemicals, as long as they export them overseas to countries where they are legally allowed to be used.

Continue reading...
items.t: European-made pesticides named in 1,605 poisoning reports in Brazil last year

items.title: Asylum seekers on final ‘one in, one out’ UK-France flight feel they are being ‘punished’
items.summary:
Many of those onboard are being deported for second time after fleeing threats from people smugglers in France

Many of the asylum seekers on Tuesday’s final “one in, one out” deportation flight are people who returned to the UK fleeing threats from smugglers after they were already forcibly returned to France.

Hundreds of asylum seekers who were sent back to France are thought to have returned to the UK, citing threats from smugglers who said their families still owed them money for the Channel crossing.

Continue reading...
items.t: Asylum seekers on final ‘one in, one out’ UK-France flight feel they are being ‘punished’

items.title: Serbia’s Student List candidates sworn in as MPs after election triumph
items.summary:
Inaugural parliamentary session comes as ousted populist Aleksandar Vučić threatens mass protests of his own

Candidates for Serbia’s Student List, the grassroots movement of political outsiders that pulled off a spectacular victory in last month’s elections over the party of the populist leader Aleksandar Vučić, are to be sworn in as MPs as they begin the process of forming a government.

The 140 candidates – among them academics, lawyers, scientists and the odd actor – will be sworn in on Tuesday during the inaugural session of the new parliament, bringing 14 years of rule by Vučić and his Serbian Progressive party (SNS) to an end.

Continue reading...
items.t: Serbia’s Student List candidates to be sworn in as MPs after election triumph

items.title: France and Malaysia upgrade ties and announce rare earths, defence cooperation deals
items.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim agreed cooperation deals on rare earths, energy and defence in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday. Macron's two-day visit, during which France and Malaysia gave their ties strategic partnership status, comes ahead of the 70th anniversary of the countries' diplomatic relations.
items.t: Macron visits Malaysia as France seeks closer defence and rare earths ties

items.title: Protests flare in Philippines over Trump's visit and planned AI hub
items.summary: Protests against President Trump's visit to the Philippines have popped up around the country, as local residents criticize a Trump administration project to build an artificial intelligence hub.
items.t: Protests against AI hub in Philippines flare ahead of Trump's visit

items.title: Trump in Asia for historic nuclear talks with China and Russia
items.summary: US President Donald Trump landed in Asia on Monday for economic talks and a planned trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on nuclear issues and the war in Ukraine. Trump also raised the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his visit.
items.t: Trump heads to Asia for historic nuclear talks with China and Russia

items.title: Rio Tinto agrees to pay US$250m to begin repairing ‘devastation’ left by Panguna mine
items.summary:
Community leader says fund gives chance to find solutions to ‘huge problems we have been living with since the days of the mine’s operation’

Anglo-Australian miner Rio Tinto has agreed to pay a quarter-of-a-billion dollars to begin the clean-up of the toxic Panguna mine site it abandoned more than three decades ago.

Panguna, once one of the world’s most profitable gold and copper mines, was shuttered in 1989 after violent protests over environmental damage and the inequitable division of the mine’s profits sparked a decade-long civil war on the Papua New Guinean island of Bougainville.

Continue reading...
items.t: Rio Tinto agrees to pay US$250m to begin repairing ‘devastation’ left by Panguna mine

items.title: France Cricket federation faces collapse after funding scandal exposed by FRANCE 24
items.summary: France's national cricket organisation is on the verge of collapse, a top administrator says, three years after an explosive FRANCE 24 investigation revealed accusations that the body was faking matches to claim funds from the International Cricket Council.
items.t: French cricket 'dying' as funding scandal prompts federation crisis

items.title: Live: Ukraine says Crimea Bridge closed after drone, missile strikes collapse road section
items.summary: The Ukrainian military said on Tuesday that the Crimea Bridge was closed to road traffic after its drone and missile strikes caused a section of road to collapse, blocking access to the Russian-occupied territory. Russian strikes in Kyiv also hit two bridges overnight from Monday, causing closures and knocking out heating and water. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
items.t: Live: Russian attacks target bridges in Kyiv, knocking out heating and water

items.title: Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda
items.summary:
Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’

Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.

The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.

Continue reading...
items.t: Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda

items.title: Russian strikes hit two key bridges in Kyiv, disrupting water and power supplies
items.summary: Russian forces struck two major bridges crossing the Dnipro River in Kyiv late Monday, damaging critical infrastructure and causing water and power cuts in parts of the Ukrainian capital, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. The attacks came as Moscow launched a wider wave of drone and missile strikes across Ukraine, including in the regions of Cherkasy and Kharkiv.
items.t: Russian strikes hit two key bridges in Kyiv, disrupting water and power supplies

items.title: Robert Pattinson lands coveted James Bond role
items.summary: Going back more than 60 years, only six actors have played James Bond, the British secret agent code-named 007. After years of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios cast 40-year-old Robert Pattinson as the leading man. Tom Hanson has the story.
items.t: Robert Pattinson lands coveted James Bond role

items.title: Africa: Trading in yuan
items.summary: The dollar has long ruled Africa's financial landscape. But as more countries turn to China's yuan, the balance of economic power could be shifting.
items.t: Africa: Trading in yuan

items.summary: Outages hit major U.S. banks, including Chase and Bank of America; United Airlines experienced a "widespread system outage."

items.summary: "I think the Ukrainians are trying to send a message to the Russians with this - 'If you hit our bridges we can hit yours,'" reports Gulliver Cragg from Kyiv.
items.t: Ukraine hits key Crimea bridge with drones

items.title: Chase outage disrupts US online banking, Zelle payments
items.summary: Users of several major US banking apps and online portals reported outages on Monday, according to the monitoring site Downdetector.com, with one institution ruling out a cyberattack as the cause. Among those affected by the outages were Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase and the popular money transfer app Zelle.
items.t: Chase outage disrupts online banking and Zelle payments in United States

items.title: Predictable: DR Congo-Rwanda rivalry spills over to Francophonie summit
items.summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Phil Clark, professor of international politics at SOAS University of London. The diplomatic crisis between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo spilling out at the Francophonie summit in Phnom Penh for all to see has exposed an unexpected shift in their relations. Clark says that "nobody expected Rwanda to back down in this way" following President Macron's request that Paul Kagame withdraw Louise Mushikiwabo's candidacy for a third term.
items.t: La Francophonie 'waning in global influence': Linguistic institutions becoming 'less important'

items.title: Europe hunts for Palantir alternatives as militaries seek to limit US dependence
items.summary: As Europe's ​defence ministries look to limit dependency on American technology and major software company Palantir Technologies for critical military functions, a growing number of firms within the region are competing for their business. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Arthur Holland Michel, journalist and researcher specialising in emerging military technologies.
items.t: Europe hunts for Palantir alternatives as militaries seek to limit US dependence

items.title: Trump says he needs funding for air traffic control after ground stop
items.summary: US ​President ​Donald Trump, pressed on a ​technology ‌failure ⁠that ‌grounded thousands of ⁠flights last week, ​on ‌Monday told reporters ‌that ​the government needed funding for upgrade ​to ​air traffic ​control equipment. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis speaks with Sheldon Jacobson, Professor of Computer Science at the University of Illinois. He explains that "the Republicans have had full control of the House and the Senate since the President came in. They controlled everything. If they needed the money and wanted the money they could have approved the money. The fact that they didn't, in the the different bills that have been passed, suggests that it's more than just money that is going on here".
items.t: Trump says he needs funding for air traffic control after ground stop

items.summary: What we know about the cause of Friday's nationwide ground stop; Trump to meet with Putin and Xi during Asia trip.

items.title: Rogue AI: California sues OpenAI over Hugging Face and other cyberattacks
items.summary: The US state of California has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI over the Hugging Face incident and other cyberattacks, accusing the ChatGPT maker of knowingly testing dangerous advanced AI models without adequate safeguards. Meanwhile, the US Commerce Department has tightened rules over the export of US technology, aiming to close a loophole around remote access to advanced AI chips.
items.t: Rogue AI: California sues OpenAI over "Hugging Face" and other cyberattacks

items.title: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
items.summary:
Countries are meeting in Geneva to negotiate rules on weapons that can select and kill targets without human intervention. But with the U.S., Russia and Israel resisting legally binding controls, campaigners fear the window to act is closing.

(Image credit: Omer Urer)
items.t: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow

items.title: U.K. mulls changing sexual consent laws after Russell Brand case
items.summary: Britain's government will consider adopting staggered ages for sexual consent in the wake of "appalling" stories of "abuse of power by powerful men."
items.t: U.K. mulls changing sexual consent laws after Russell Brand case

items.title: Nvidia scandal: China's chips dilemma, US rivalry shape AI race
items.summary: The controversy surrounding Nvidia and its former CEO Jensen Huang has put a spotlight on the intensifying AI race between the US and China.
items.t: Nvidia scandal: China's chips dilemma, US rivalry shape AI race

items.summary: Women who have received a caution from police will also be pardoned, and women arrested or investigated for ending their own pregnancy will have those details removed from their criminal records.
items.t: Women in U.K. are getting automatic pardons for past abortion convictions

items.summary: President Trump said he may meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un on his China trip this week.

items.summary: Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, the architect of modern Mexican drug trafficking, was known as "the boss of bosses."

items.title: Guinea's gold rush: Arrests, deportations spark outcry
items.summary: Guinea has banned illegal gold mining, citing environmental concerns. It has further charged hundreds of suspected local and foreign illegal miners amid reports of rights abuses and deportations.
items.t: Guinea's gold rush: Arrests, deportations spark outcry

items.title: Civilian U.S. medics in Kuwait attack describe drone strike chaos, lack of preparation
items.summary: Norah O'Donnell spoke with U.S. civilian medics for "60 Minutes" about the deadly drone strike on a U.S. base in Kuwait at the start of the Iran war. They described a lack of preparation ahead of the attack.
items.t: Civilian U.S. medics in Kuwait attack describe drone strike chaos, lack of preparation

items.title: US basketball player arrested with 75lb of marijuana at Nigerian airport, say authorities
items.summary:
• Suspect named as Greene Da’monte Khiree

  • Drug smuggling carries life sentence in Nigeria

An American basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria for allegedly attempting to smuggle 33.95kg (75lb) of marijuana into the country.

Nigeria’s National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said a 28-year-old player named as Greene Da’monte Khiree from the state of Georgia was arrested at Lagos’s main airport last Wednesday after he arrived on a flight from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates.

Continue reading...
items.t: US basketball player arrested with 75lb of marijuana at Nigerian airport, say authorities

items.title: Basketball player allegedly had 75 pounds of drugs in luggage
items.summary: Nigeria's anti-narcotics agency said it had arrested an American professional basketball player with 33.95 kilograms of cannabis in his luggage on arrival at the main airport.
items.t: Basketball player allegedly had 75 pounds of drugs in luggage

items.title: Ukraine hits Kerch bridge between Russia and occupied Crimea
items.summary:
Traffic temporarily restricted on key connection after bridge targeted during overnight drone barrage by Ukraine

Ukraine has hit the Kerch bridge connecting occupied Crimea with Russia, in a symbolic blow that temporarily paralysed road traffic and left thousands of drivers stranded.

A Ukrainian kamikaze drone crashed into one of the bridge’s arches at 5.38am local time, local channels reported. Earlier drones could be heard buzzing above the structure, as Russian air defence units opened fire.

Continue reading...
items.t: Ukraine hits Kerch bridge between Russia and occupied Crimea

items.title: FAA ground stop still affecting thousands of flights. And, Trump meets Xi, Putin in Asia
items.summary:
U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that things could be back to normal at the end of Monday after an FAA ground stop disrupted flights. And, Trump heads to Asia for a high-profile trilateral summit.

(Image credit: Aaron Schwartz)
items.t: FAA ground stop still affecting thousands of flights. And, Trump meets Xi, Putin in Asia

items.title: Chris Van Hollen says he can beat Chuck Schumer. Here's his case
items.summary:
Sen. Chris Van Hollen told NPR's Morning Edition why he believes he can defeat Sen. Chuck Schumer and what he would change about Senate Democratic leadership.

(Image credit: Mark Makela)
items.t: Chris Van Hollen says he can beat Chuck Schumer. Here's his case

items.title: Eurovision organisers criticise Malaysian removal of LGBT+ footage in first Asian contest
items.summary:
Broadcaster TV3 appears to cut footage of Thai drag performers and gay Philippine jury spokesperson

Eurovision’s organisers have said they are “surprised and disappointed” that the first Eurovision Asia was altered when it was broadcast in Malaysia, apparently removing LGBTQ+ imagery and people from the show.

The European Broadcasting Union (EBU), the alliance of public broadcasters that owns Eurovision, said it would write to Voxovation, the company producing the Asian contest under licence, and ask it to establish with the Malaysian broadcaster TV3 why it happened.

Continue reading...
items.t: Eurovision organisers criticise Malaysian removal of LGBT+ footage in first Asian contest

items.title: Trump to embark on Asia trip in apparent foreign policy push before end of term
items.summary:
Experts say US president may lean toward global affairs after domestic influence curtailed in midterm elections

Donald Trump is embarking on his first overseas trip since his Republican party’s thumping midterm repudiation by US voters, in what may herald a renewed focus on foreign policy for the remainder of his presidency.

The US president will meet his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, for their first trilateral summit, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) forum in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. Before that, he will land in Manila in the Philippines on Tuesday for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit.

Continue reading...
items.t: Trump to embark on Asia trip in apparent foreign policy push before end of term

items.title: Jordan bans Telegram app over 'radicalisation' claims
items.summary: Jordan has imposed a ban on Telegram over a deadly church attack which left seven people dead. Iraq later followed with a partial ban to compel the company to review its content.
items.t: Jordan bans Telegram app over 'radicalisation' claims

items.title: Relocation of Cape Town baboons to sanctuary ignites heated protests
items.summary:
Demonstrators tried to block vehicle carrying the baboons, whose capture authorities say is needed to protect both primate and human

The relocation of a troop of baboons in Cape Town to a wildlife sanctuary has triggered furious protests by local people opposed to their capture, which officials argue is necessary to stop human-wildlife conflict in the city.

The 44-member Waterfall troop (named after the area they mainly inhabit) was captured in the southern seaside suburb of Simon’s Town on Friday and Saturday. A second, smaller Seaforth troop is also due to be moved.

Continue reading...
items.t: Relocation of Cape Town baboons to sanctuary ignites heated protests

items.title: Trump heads to Asia to meet with Xi and Putin amid Nvidia fallout
items.summary:
The trip to China marks Trump's second time this year, and comes as the president and his party faced widespread backlash from voters in the recent midterm elections.

(Image credit: Kevin Dietsch)
items.t: Trump heads to Asia to meet with Xi and Putin amid Nvidia fallout

items.title: Delaware hit by rare November tornado
items.summary:
Meanwhile, severe thunderstorms bring hailstones the size of baseballs in Argentina

The National Weather Service in the US has confirmed that an EF1 tornado touched down south-east of Newark in the Salem Woods neighbourhood, Delaware, on Thursday. The tornado reached 160 metres wide, had a path length of 4.4 miles (7.1km) and reached estimated peak winds of up to 100mph (161km/h). There were no injuries or fatalities but windows and roofs were damaged on several homes, a large hotel sign fell on to a number of cars, and a semi truck overturned on I95. Although Delaware often experiences a few tornadoes every year, this is only the second time the state has had tornado activity in November since 1950, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The only other November tornado recorded was in 1989.

Severe storms have also resulted in tornadoes in Argentina as well as large hailstones. A round of severe thunderstorms moved through the central Córdoba province on Friday, bringing hailstones up to the size of a baseball (about 7.5cm in diameter). Parts of the province recorded up to 73mm of rainfall in just six hours early on Saturday. Such storms are common at this time of year. Water vapour from the Amazon meeting the Andes quickly condenses, resulting in massive cloud formations often associated with heavy downpours, lightning, tornadoes and large hailstones.

items.title: Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe
items.summary:
Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week

Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.

After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Further heavy rain is expected to fall in Italy and the Balkans over the next few days, with the latest forecast models indicating an additional 100mm could accumulate widely, while totals close to 200mm are likely in more mountainous areas.

items.t: Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe
